title: Before-LCM (Laser-Capture Microdissection) Procedure
author: Aisha M Basudan
materials: Laboratory surfaces and equipment should be decontaminated by wiping down with a commercially RNase decontamination solution,a mild solution of bleach, or NaOH, followed by wiping with absolute ethanol, and then rinsing twice with nuclease-free water.

Chemical reagents and solutions are either certified as RNase-freeby the manufacturer, treated with diethylpyrocarbonate (DEPC). In addition, RNase inhibitor, for example SUPERase In™ RNase Inhibitor,ProtectRNA RNaseInhibitor, or RNasin® Plus RNase Inhibitor, could be added to the used solutions. All solutions should not be reused or poured back into their containers.

Immediately after specimen dissection cool down isopentane (2-methylbutane, Sigma-Aldrich, St Louis, USA) by slowly pouring it into a container with dry ice. It is ready for use once the isopentane bubbling subsides.
To minimize RNase activity, add 50 µL of ProtectRNA (ProtectRNA™ RNase inhibitor 500 x-concentrates, Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, USA) to each jar except the one containing xylene.

steps.title: Establish RNase‑free environment
steps.instruction: Wear disposable gloves at all times and change them frequently; decontaminate all glassware and metalware or bake them at 450 °F (230 °C) for at least 2 h; use only RNase‑free certified plastic ware – if reused, rinse with absolute ethanol, then distilled water, treat with commercial RNase‑decontamination solution, rinse with nuclease‑free water, and dry in a hood; dip slides in the same RNase‑decontamination solution for a few seconds, wash twice with nuclease‑free water, dry for 2 h at 37‑55 °C, and give a brief UV‑treatment immediately before use.

substeps.instruction: Wear disposable gloves and change frequently.
Decontaminate glassware/metalware or bake at 450 °F (230 °C) for ≥2 h.
Rinse reusable plastic ware with absolute ethanol, distilled water, treat with RNase‑decontamination solution, rinse with nuclease‑free water, dry in hood.
Dip slides in RNase‑decontamination solution for a few seconds, wash twice with nuclease‑free water, dry 2 h at 37‑55 °C, UV‑treat shortly before use.

steps.title: Euthanize rats and dissect MCC
steps.instruction: Sacrifice 5‑week‑old male Sprague‑Dawley rats by intraperitoneal injection of 20 % Dorminal (200 mg pentobarbital sodium, Alfasan, Woerden‑Holland, Netherlands) at 100 mg per 100 g body weight; immediately aseptically remove mandibular condyles with part of the ramus, discarding all muscle and periosteum while keeping a minimal bone rim, using a Vuemax‑Pro head magnifier with light (China).

steps.title: Prepare cryomold and embed tissue
steps.instruction: Label a Tissue‑Tek Biopsy Cryomold (10 × 10 × 5 mm or 15 × 15 × 5 mm, Sakura Finetek, USA) and add a thin layer of Tissue‑Tek OCT compound (optimal cutting temperature grade, Sakura Finetek, USA) to the bottom; cool the mold in a dry‑ice container, then place the dissected MCC specimen onto the OCT, orient with RNase‑free tweezers so the region of interest faces up (both right and left MCC may be placed in the same mold).

steps.title: Cover specimen with OCT and freeze
steps.instruction: Add OCT until the specimen is completely covered, avoiding bubbles (remove any bubbles with a pipette tip or thin needle); immediately plunge the mold into cooled isopentane until the OCT turns white (a few minutes). If not proceeding immediately, store the frozen block in the cryomold at –70 °C.

steps.title: Set up cryostat and prepare chamber
steps.instruction: Set the Reichert‑Jung Cryocut 1800 cryostat (Cambridge Instruments, Germany) to –24 °C to –30 °C; prepare microslide boxes with either plain uncharged or coated charged glass slides as per the RNase‑free technique; remove the old microtome blade, wipe the chamber, anti‑roll plate and knife holder with 100 % ethanol, install a new blade, and transfer the OCT‑embedded block from the –70 °C freezer into the cryostat to equilibrate; treat all metal ware (specimen stage, tweezers) and brushes with the RNase‑free protocol and place them inside the chamber to cool.

steps.title: Mount block and mount sections
steps.instruction: Inside the cryostat, remove the frozen OCT block from the mold and mount it securely to the specimen stage with OCT medium; let the OCT harden and attach the stage to the holder; place an empty microslide box with a small Drierite desiccant pack on dry ice near the cryostat.

steps.title: Section tissue and collect on slides
steps.instruction: Trim excess OCT by cutting at 10‑20 µm; when approaching the tissue, set the cutting thickness to 7 µm; mount each section onto the central area of a HistoBond®+ adhesive microscope slide (Marienfeld, Germany). Keep slides at room temperature, but after the first section keep the slide in the cryostat until all sections are placed. Multiple sections (up to six MCC sections per slide) may be mounted to reduce handling; work quickly to avoid RNA degradation and prevent sections from drying on the slide.

steps.title: Store slides and create guide map
steps.instruction: Place slides with cryosections in a chilled slide box (capacity 20‑25 slides) on dry ice; when full, seal with Parafilm “M” (American National Can, Chicago, USA) and store at –70 °C. Use one stained cryosection as a guide map for every tenth slide. Discard the first and last ten slides (very small sections); the middle 30‑40 slides provide reliable MCC zone identification.

steps.title: Prepare staining and dehydration solutions
steps.instruction: After cleaning the staining and dehydration jars, fill each jar with 25 ml of the appropriate solution as per the Arcturus HistoGene‱ LCM Frozen Section Staining Kit (CA, USA) instructions: RNase‑free water, 75 % ethanol, 50 % ethanol, 25 % ethanol, and absolute ethanol. Add Molecular‑sieve 4 Å desiccant beads (Sigma‑Aldrich, Strinheim, Germany) to the absolute ethanol jar and to the xylene jar to prevent rehydration. Place the 75 % ethanol jar in a –20 °C freezer; keep the remaining jars on ice or in a –4 °C freezer.

steps.title: Thaw slide and perform dehydration
steps.instruction: Remove one slide (six sections) from the –80 °C freezer and defrost for less than 30 seconds or until the corners are thawed; using RNase‑free forceps, transfer the slide sequentially through the jars (RNase‑free water → 75 % ethanol → 50 % ethanol → 25 % ethanol → absolute ethanol), blot excess liquid after each transfer to avoid carry‑over. If staining is not required, skip the staining step and the subsequent water wash. After the first absolute ethanol immersion, place the slide in a second absolute ethanol jar for an additional 2 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Transfer through RNase‑free water and ethanol series, blot after each step.
Skip staining and water wash if not needed.
Incubate in second absolute ethanol jar for 2 min.

steps.title: Final dehydration and proceed to LCM
steps.instruction: Continue with the manufacturer’s xylene dehydration and air‑drying steps, then immediately begin laser‑capture microdissection. Process one slide at a time to minimise RNA degradation.
